selected.why_today: The latest registry update describes an active Texas trial with a tangible daily task; full protocol inspection adds authentic examples and an explicit diagnostic limit.

filmability.viewer_question: Can the phone you already carry provide a usable fetal-movement recording?
filmability.opening_action: Reveal the protocol screenshot of the app recording interface, then its quiet-room instruction and clinical caution.
filmability.mechanism: The smartphone records audio; uploaded audio is analyzed at TACC; participants receive experimental movement analysis in the app.
filmability.human_consequence: Participants must sustain usable recordings while researchers assess feasibility and anxiety; experimental output cannot establish fetal health
filmability.source_limit: Recruiting feasibility study, not a proven diagnostic or prevention tool. Screenshots are July 31 protocol examples; registry updated September 14. No results posted.

action_support.pictured_action: Reveal the protocol screenshot of the app recording interface, then its quiet-room instruction and clinical caution.
action_support.scope_fit: Authentic static source example of the daily task; focus reveals can emphasize existing words without inventing user interaction.

action_support.pictured_action: Build a three-node relationship from phone recording through TACC analysis back to movement categories in the app.
action_support.scope_fit: Explain only the data flow expressly described in the live registration; no simulated fetus, waveform, clinical score or detection event.
action_support.relationship: The smartphone records audio; uploaded audio is analyzed at TACC; participants receive experimental movement analysis in the app.

action_support.pictured_action: Reveal the actual Recording Failed screen and the source notice that handling noise can require another recording.
action_support.scope_fit: Shows a documented design limit, not a claimed frequency or an observed participant event. End with the experimental-use boundary.

visual_stakes.affected_person: Pregnant participants enrolled through Dell Medical School, UTHealth Houston and UTMB Galveston
visual_stakes.physical_subject: A smartphone microphone held against the abdomen during a daily recording
visual_stakes.visible_change: The source app examples move the viewer from a recording interface to a failed-recording notice caused by handling noise
visual_stakes.consequence: Participants must sustain usable recordings while researchers assess feasibility and anxiety; experimental output cannot establish fetal health
visual_stakes.opening_question: Can the phone you already carry provide a usable fetal-movement recording?
visual_stakes.answer: Texas researchers are testing daily recordings and AI analysis; the study has no posted results and its consent says the app is experimental
visual_stakes.asset_fit: The protocol supplies authentic recording, error and caution screens. One simple sourced flow diagram can explain where the AI runs.

selected.consequence: Participants must repeat unusable recordings while researchers measure whether daily research use is practical.
selected.application_change: A phone microphone supplies recordings for an AI research model, with output returned inside an experimental app.
selected.counter_image: The actual protocol shows a failed recording and explicitly says results are experimental and not diagnostic.
selected.earned_take: Obtaining a recording and interpreting it as a clinical answer are separate tasks; this study is testing the former workflow.

agency.next_step: Investigators continue recruitment and assess usability and participant anxiety during daily app use.
agency.who_can_act: The listed study teams and eligible enrolled participants.
